name: Carolina Bird Club Conservation Grants
summary: Small grants from a birding club for conservation actions that address the needs of a bird species or group of species in the Carolinas, applied for by a conservation organisation. Construction work is generally excluded.
reporting: A final report with an accounting of expenditures and a project summary, within 30 days of completion.

eligibility.rule: Student research projects have faculty sponsorship
No institutional indirect costs or general operational costs

documents: Faculty sponsor or school principal support letter, when applicable
Research start date and funding period
Grant purpose, actions, affected species and area
Project plans with dates, when appropriate

status.quote: Grant applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

applicant_types.quote: An official representative of the conservation organization should send an application

geography.quote: The CBC provides grants to support research, education and conservation of birds of the Carolinas and their habitats.

access.quote: Email completed applications or inquiries to: Grants Committee

window.quote: Grant applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

reporting.quote: Awardees must file a final report including an accounting of expenditures and a summary of the completed project no later than 30 days following its completion.

effort.quote: Email completed applications or inquiries to: Grants Committee

eligibility.quote: For student research projects, applications require the sponsorship of a faculty member.
The Carolina Bird Club does not support institutional indirect costs, or fund general operational costs of an organization.

after_award.quote: Awardees must file a final report including an accounting of expenditures

documents.quote: A scope of work (limited to two single-spaced pages), including species to be studied and the site where the work will be conducted.

A detailed budget. Appropriate course work and other activities that would indicate that the applicant is capable of performing the described research. A letter of support from the faculty sponsor or school principal. Details of the starting date of the research and the time period for which funding is requested. The name of the payee and the address to which a check should be mailed.

Details of the purpose of the grant request; action(s) to be undertaken, species or groups of species affected, acres/units affected. Identify the conservation need of the species or group of species for which actions are proposed Detailed Budget. Project plans (with dates) as appropriate.
